title: PopFetcher: Towards Accelerated Mixture-of-Experts Training Via Popularity Based Expert-Wise Prefetch
problem: Mixture-of-Experts training suffers from substantial All-to-All communications and imbalanced computation workloads due to sparse expert activation, severely degrading training efficiency.
motivation: Efficient MoE training is critical to scaling large language models to trillions of parameters while maintaining practical computational overhead.
method: PopFetcher predicts expert popularity using a lightweight sliding-window technique to identify high-demand experts, then prefetches them asynchronously during non-MoE computations. It formulates end-to-end training latency as an optimization problem with a pruning strategy to derive the globally optimal prefetching scheme, while prioritizing All-to-All communication during the backward pass.
key_novelty: Popularity-aided prefetching with formally-optimized pruning strategy derived from end-to-end training latency model.
contributions: Uncovers skewed and correlated patterns in expert selection within MoE models
Develops lightweight sliding-window technique for predicting expert popularity
Formulates end-to-end training latency and derives optimal prefetching strategy via pruning
Achieves 15%-94.5% training time reduction on GPU clusters
primary_theme: Popularity-based prefetching for MoE training acceleration
